title: What are the pros and cons of living in a city?🏙️: Real Easy English

sentences.en: Hello, I'm Neil.
sentences.ko: 안녕하세요, 저는 닐이에요.

sentences.en: And I'm Georgie.
sentences.ko: 그리고 저는 조지예요.

sentences.en: Welcome to Real Easy English.
sentences.ko: Real Easy English에 오신 걸 환영해요.

sentences.en: You can find a worksheet and transcript for this episode on our website, bbclearningenglish.com
sentences.ko: 이 에피소드의 학습지와 대본은 웹사이트 bbclearningenglish.com에서 볼 수 있어요.

sentences.en: Hello Neil. How are you doing?
sentences.ko: 안녕, 닐. 어떻게 지내요?

sentences.en: I'm very well, thank you, Georgie. How are you?
sentences.ko: 아주 잘 지내요, 고마워요, 조지. 당신은요?

sentences.en: Yes, I'm very well, thank you. Neil, today we're talking about cities.
sentences.ko: 네, 아주 잘 지내요, 고마워요. 닐, 오늘은 도시에 대해 얘기해요.

sentences.en: We both live and work in London, which is a very big city.
sentences.ko: 우리 둘 다 아주 큰 도시인 런던에서 살고 일하죠.

sentences.en: It is. It's a huge city – very busy and bustling.
sentences.ko: 그렇죠. 거대한 도시예요. 아주 바쁘고 북적거려요(bustling).

sentences.en: Bustling means there's lots of activity, lots of things going on, busy.
sentences.ko: Bustling은 활동이 많고, 일이 많이 벌어지고, 분주하다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.en: Speaking of, what do you like about living in a big, bustling city?
sentences.ko: 말 나온 김에, 크고 북적이는 도시에 사는 게 뭐가 좋아요?

sentences.en: Well, there are lots of good things about living in a big city.
sentences.ko: 음, 큰 도시에 살면 좋은 점이 많아요.

sentences.en: It's convenient.
sentences.ko: 편리해요.

sentences.en: It's very convenient.
sentences.ko: 아주 편리해요.

sentences.en: So, there is lots of public transport, which is sometimes good.
sentences.ko: 대중교통이 많은데, 그게 좋을 때가 있어요.

sentences.en: And you can get things that you need quite easily.
sentences.ko: 그리고 필요한 걸 꽤 쉽게 구할 수 있어요.

sentences.en: That's very true.
sentences.ko: 정말 맞아요.

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.ko: 네.

sentences.en: Yeah. There's also a lot of things to do.
sentences.ko: 네. 할 것도 정말 많아요.

sentences.en: We are lucky in London to have lots of theatres where you can see plays.
sentences.ko: 런던엔 연극을 볼 수 있는 극장이 많아서 운이 좋아요.

sentences.en: There's a really good music scene, so you can watch and listen to a lot of live music.
sentences.ko: 음악 문화도 정말 좋아서 라이브 음악을 많이 보고 들을 수 있어요.

sentences.en: If you have no plans on a day, you can always find plans, spontaneous plans, so we are really lucky in that sense.
sentences.ko: 어느 날 계획이 없어도 언제든 즉흥적인 계획을 세울 수 있으니, 그런 면에서 정말 운이 좋아요.

sentences.en: Yeah, and if you like art, there's all kinds of exhibitions and galleries and museums.
sentences.ko: 네, 그리고 미술을 좋아하면 온갖 전시회와 갤러리와 박물관이 있죠.

sentences.en: Lots of good things.
sentences.ko: 좋은 게 많아요.

sentences.en: But there are obviously some bad things about living in a city, aren't there?
sentences.ko: 그런데 도시에 살면 당연히 안 좋은 점도 있죠?

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.ko: 네.

sentences.en: Do you want to tell us some?
sentences.ko: 몇 가지 말해 줄래요?

sentences.en: Yeah. Well, it's very noisy and dirty...
sentences.ko: 네. 음, 아주 시끄럽고 더럽고...

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.ko: 그렇죠.

sentences.en: ...and busy and expensive.
sentences.ko: ...붐비고 비싸요.

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.ko: 네.

sentences.en: It's always more expensive in a big city, especially the capital city.
sentences.ko: 큰 도시, 특히 수도는 늘 더 비싸요.

sentences.en: So, you can do all of the things that we just talked about...
sentences.ko: 그러니까 방금 얘기한 것들을 다 할 수 있지만...

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.ko: 네.

sentences.en: ...but you have to pay for them.
sentences.ko: ...돈을 내야 하죠.

sentences.en: Yeah!
sentences.ko: 맞아요!

sentences.en: And things like eating out, especially going for a drink, is a really expensive thing to do in the capital city.
sentences.ko: 외식, 특히 술 한잔하러 가는 건 수도에서 정말 비싼 일이에요.

sentences.en: I feel like every time I leave the house I just spend loads of money and that is quite frustrating, but you have to pay for good...
sentences.ko: 집을 나설 때마다 돈을 왕창 쓰는 것 같아서 꽤 속상해요. 그래도 좋은...

sentences.en: for good times, I guess.
sentences.ko: 좋은 시간을 보내려면 돈을 내야 하는 거겠죠.

sentences.en: Yeah. Have you ever lived in another city apart from London?
sentences.ko: 네. 런던 말고 다른 도시에 살아 본 적 있어요?

sentences.en: Yes, I have.
sentences.ko: 네, 있어요.

sentences.en: I used to live in Barcelona, which is quite different to London because, well, it has a beach and the sea on one side and on the other side it has mountains, so it's contained by nature and you can get to the nature quite quickly,
sentences.ko: 예전에 바르셀로나에 살았는데, 런던과는 꽤 달라요. 한쪽엔 해변과 바다가 있고 다른 쪽엔 산이 있어서 자연에 둘러싸여 있고, 자연으로 꽤 빨리 갈 수 있어요.

sentences.en: which is really nice.
sentences.ko: 그게 정말 좋아요.

sentences.en: What about you? Have you lived anywhere different?
sentences.ko: 당신은요? 다른 곳에 살아 본 적 있어요?

sentences.en: Yeah, I've lived in a few big cities – a few capital cities, actually.
sentences.ko: 네, 큰 도시 몇 군데, 사실 수도 몇 군데에 살아 봤어요.

sentences.en: I've also lived in Spain, but in Madrid.
sentences.ko: 저도 스페인에 살았는데, 마드리드였어요.

sentences.en: I lived and worked in Prague and that is a really pretty...
sentences.ko: 프라하에서 살면서 일했는데, 정말 예쁜...

sentences.en: it's a beautiful city.
sentences.ko: 아름다운 도시예요.

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.ko: 네.

sentences.en: The architecture looks fantastic.
sentences.ko: 건축물이 환상적이에요.

sentences.en: Nice buildings. Talking about nice buildings, I lived in Edinburgh because I did my master's degree there and that has beautiful buildings.
sentences.ko: 멋진 건물들이요. 멋진 건물 얘기가 나왔으니, 에든버러에서 석사 과정을 해서 거기 살았는데, 건물들이 아름다워요.

sentences.en: I loved that city.
sentences.ko: 그 도시가 정말 좋았어요.

sentences.en: It has a castle on a big rock in the middle and it's just amazing to look at.
sentences.ko: 한가운데 큰 바위 위에 성이 있는데, 보기만 해도 정말 멋져요.

sentences.en: So, we've talked about cities we've been to.
sentences.ko: 우리가 가 본 도시들에 대해 얘기했는데요.

sentences.en: What about the future?
sentences.ko: 앞으로는요?

sentences.en: Are there any cities you really want to visit or maybe even live in?
sentences.ko: 꼭 가 보고 싶거나 살아 보고 싶은 도시가 있어요?

sentences.en: Oh, that's an interesting question!
sentences.ko: 오, 흥미로운 질문이네요!

sentences.en: I've never been to Georgia or Armenia or that part of the world, so I'm going to say I'd like to go to Tbilisi in Georgia.
sentences.ko: 조지아나 아르메니아, 그쪽 지역엔 가 본 적이 없어서, 조지아의 트빌리시에 가 보고 싶다고 할게요.

sentences.en: That's a good answer. I'd love to go there as well.
sentences.ko: 좋은 답이네요. 저도 거기 정말 가 보고 싶어요.

sentences.en: For me, I'm desperate to go to Latin America.
sentences.ko: 저는 라틴 아메리카에 정말 너무 가고 싶어요.

sentences.en: I really want to go to Rio de Janeiro, and at the time when the carnival is there, because that sounds really fun and I like to party!
sentences.ko: 리우데자네이루에 꼭 가 보고 싶어요. 카니발 기간에요. 정말 재밌을 것 같고, 저는 파티를 좋아하거든요!

sentences.en: Let's recap the vocabulary we heard during the conversation, starting with bustling, which means busy with lots of people and activity.
sentences.ko: 대화에서 들은 어휘를 정리해 봐요. bustling부터요. 사람과 활동이 많아 분주하다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.en: We also heard convenient.
sentences.ko: convenient도 나왔어요.

sentences.en: If something is convenient, it means it's very easy to do it.
sentences.ko: 뭔가가 convenient하면 하기가 아주 쉽다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.en: For example, there's lots of public transport in London, so it's convenient for travel.
sentences.ko: 예를 들어 런던엔 대중교통이 많아서 이동하기 편리해요.

sentences.en: And we talked about possible plans for the future, using would like to.
sentences.ko: 그리고 would like to를 써서 앞으로의 계획에 대해 얘기했어요.

sentences.en: For example, I'd like to visit Tbilisi in Georgia.
sentences.ko: 예를 들면 'I'd like to visit Tbilisi in Georgia.'

sentences.en: That's it for this episode of Real Easy English, but we'll be back next week with another conversation in easy English.
sentences.ko: Real Easy English 이번 에피소드는 여기까지예요. 다음 주에 쉬운 영어로 된 다른 대화로 돌아올게요.

sentences.en: And you should check out our series The London to Edinburgh Challenge.
sentences.ko: 그리고 저희 시리즈 'The London to Edinburgh Challenge'도 꼭 보세요.

sentences.en: We've been talking about Edinburgh today.
sentences.ko: 오늘 에든버러 얘기를 했잖아요.

sentences.en: It's a beautiful place and you can see it in this series.
sentences.ko: 아름다운 곳인데, 이 시리즈에서 볼 수 있어요.

sentences.en: It's on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.ko: 웹사이트 bbclearningenglish.com에 있어요.

sentences.en: Goodbye for now.
sentences.ko: 오늘은 여기까지, 안녕히.

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.ko: 안녕!
